title: Autoscale Steering Controller for Multi‑Fidelity Workloads — PRD (draft)
body:
Purpose
This doc describes a proposed Autoscale Steering Controller (ASC) that dynamically adjusts dedicated-pool scaling and burst allocations based on per-tenant workload fidelity (latency vs quality), cost sensitivity, and isolation requirements. The ASC is intended to sit between the traffic-level scaler (node/pod autoscaler) and the tenant allocation policies to provide smarter, workload-aware decisions for Dedicated capacity.

Context and motivation
- Problem: tenants run mixed workloads (short low-cost queries, long high-fidelity reasoning chains, embeddings batch jobs). Current autoscalers treat all requests the same which causes: wasted warm GPU memory, poor tail latency for latency-sensitive requests, and unfair burst exhaustion for long-running tenants.
- Goal: preserve latency SLOs for latency-sensitive lanes, preserve model-quality SLOs for fidelity-sensitive lanes, and improve overall cluster utilization and unit cost.
- Constraints: must be safe for Dedicated (no noisy-neighbor regressions), compatible with existing fallback lanes and burst credits, and operable by SREs/product without heavy manual tuning.

High-level approach
- Introduce an Autoscale Steering Controller (ASC) with three input surfaces: (1) real‑time telemetry (latency percentiles, queue length, KV cache hit rate), (2) tenant workload profile (fidelity tags, cost class, reservation size), (3) external signals (scheduled events, forecasted demand).
- ASC outputs: recommended scale actions (scale-up intensity, preferred pool for new allocs, prewarm hints) and a per-tenant steering decision (route to hot pool, degraded fidelity pool, or queued/burst lane).
- Steering is advisory to the autoscaler/dispatcher; enforcement happens via token-lane assignment and soft-isolation gates.

Key concepts (novel pieces)
1) Fidelity buckets — label traffic by inferred fidelity need (FAST, BALANCED, DEEP) derived from model, prompt markers, token horizon, and past latency/quality signals. These are soft tags attached to requests and used as first-class inputs to scaling.
2) Steering score — continuous score per tenant-workload computed from cost-sensitivity, recent tail latency, KV locality, and credit balance. Higher score => aggressive allocation to hot GPUs.
3) Predictive warm windows — when a tenant's forecasted steering score crosses a threshold, ASC schedules prewarm tasks to seed KV caches and model weights on candidate nodes. This reduces cold-start tail.
4) Cross‑tenant isolation fences — soft admission controllers that dynamically tighten concurrency limits for tenants whose steering score drops while expanding headroom for high-score tenants. This avoids hard evictions.
5) Burst-tranche routing — instead of single global burst pool, bursts are served from small per-fidelity tranches to reduce cross-impact (e.g., FAST-burst tranche for short queries, DEEP-burst for long jobs).

Detailed mechanics
- Inputs and metrics used: p50/p90/p99 latency per route; request token length histogram; KV cache hit ratio; per-tenant burst-credit ledger; GPU occupancy and memory fragmentation; pending queue depth; rolling 10m traffic forecasts.
- Scoring function (sketch): steering_score = w1*latency_risk + w2*kv_locality + w3*(credit_balance/commit_size) + w4*cost_priority + w5*forecast_delta. Tunable weights with safe defaults.
- Decision thresholds: three bands -> allow-prewarm, allow-burst, throttled-queue. Bands calibrated per pool size and SLOs.
- Interaction with existing autoscalers: ASC provides a prioritized list of scale intents (nodes to spin up with suggested labels: e.g., hot-fidelity=FAST). Cluster autoscaler still makes final decisions; ASC can optionally take over in emergency mode.

API surface (operator facing)
- New API: POST /v1/dedicated/steering/recommendation { tenant_id, time_horizon, risk_profile } -> { recommendations: [ { pool_label, prewarm: bool, burst_tranche: id, suggested_replicas_delta } ], ttl }
- Config: per-tenant steering policy objects in product console (json blob): { fidelity_preferences, max_prewarms_per_hour, burst_tranche_preference, isolation_sensitivity }

Safety and graceful degradation
- Safety: all steering outputs are advisory by default. Enforcement requires operator opt-in. Introduce conservative defaults (no prewarm unless forecast confidence > 0.8).
- Rollback: ASC can be throttled to passive mode (recommendations only visible in console).
- Fallback: if ASC fails, revert to existing autoscaler with last-known safe config and drain prewarm nodes.

Operational observability
- Dashboards: per-tenant steering score timelines, prewarm success rate (cache warm hit delta), burst-tranche exhaustion heatmap, scale-action latency.
- Alerts: sudden drop in p99 for FAST lanes, prewarm failure > 5% in 1h, steering-service CPU/mem spike.
- Playbooks: escalate to SRE if steering causes >5% SLO regression within 30 minutes; steps include disabling scheduler, draining prewarm nodes, and reverting per-tenant policy.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Lab: implement ASC simulation harness that reads historical telemetry and runs recommendations offline. Validate with traces (2w).
2) Canary (internal tenants only): expose advisory recommendations to ops console for a handful of mid-size tenants (2w). Monitor fidelity SLOs and prewarm ROI.
3) Opt-in beta: allow 10 paying tenants to enable ASC enforcement in a single region. Track cost delta and SLO impact (4–6w).
4) Gradual ramp: enable for low-risk fidelity lanes globally, expand controls.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Weight tuning: who owns production tuning of steering_score weights? Suggest product+applied-ml initial and eng-sre for runbook.
- Billing implications: does prewarm time count toward committed capacity for Dedicated contracts? Legal/finance input needed.
- Data retention and privacy: steering uses request metadata; confirm allowed retention window for PII-sensitive tenants.
- Tenant config UX: console needs a simple UX for fidelity preferences that maps to our three buckets. Design input required.

Implementation notes / rough timeline
- M1: prototype scoring engine + simulation harness (4w) — eng-applied-ml + serving-runtime
- M2: ASC service + scheduler plugin + console prototype (6w) — platform-eng + console-and-tooling
- M3: safe rollout features (passive/advisory mode, throttles, metrics) (3w) — sre + product
- M4: beta to tenants and feedback loop (6–8w)

Short-term TODOs
- [ ] Wire up sample dataset and run offline simulation on last 30d of dedicated telemetry (assigned: Omar)
- [ ] Draft console UX mockups for tenant fidelity preferences (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Spike prewarm runner prototype to test KV reuse across tenants (assigned: Liam)
- [ ] Add Linear tickets for testing scenarios and create evaluation criteria for success

Notes to self / informal thoughts
- Might be useful to let tenants tag a route as HIGH_QUALITY_REQUIRED in API call headers; makes fidelity inference explicit. Add to API proposal.
- Consider marketplace model later: tenants could sell unused prewarm slots, but keep that for a follow-up — risk of complexity.
- Keep default behavior conservative: the platform must never reduce isolation guarantees unless explicitly enabled by tenant or enterprise admin.

References and links
- Sim harness proto: github.com/redwood-inference/sim/auto-steer-proto
- Related tickets: DE-812, DE-847, OPS-192
- Slack thread: #dedicated-autoscale (see thread ts 2024-10-18)

Appendix: example per-tenant policy (simple)
- tenant_id: acme-corp
- fidelity_preferences: [FAST: 0.7, BALANCED: 0.2, DEEP: 0.1]
- max_concurrent_prewarms: 3
- burst_tranche_preference: FAST,BALANCED
- isolation_sensitivity: medium

End of draft — feedback requested from applied-ml, eng-sre, and platform-eng
